C-ACCEPTANCE-REGISTRY.IntentSummary: One JSON authority + one survey ledger + a validator in the standard test matrix + a builder that reproduces the isolated-artifact procedure; backfilled with the live 2.6.x-next wave so the registry opens already answering "what is where, accepted or not, and why".

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: registry.json validates: artifacts keyed by id with source sha/branch, platform, bundle identity, binary digest, builtAt, covers[], location, status; items keyed by delivery id with an ordered events[] (state, date, actor, detail) covering reported/repaired/reviewed waves/artifact offers/owner verdicts; the 2.6.x-next wave complete per the spec acceptance list.

README states the lifecycle (mirroring the train stage table), artifact requirements (isolated identity, no updater artifacts, digest, smoke), verdict rules (exact scenarios; rejection reason + rework destination; partial acceptance allowed; never inferred), and a survey table generated from the registry state.

tools/acceptance-registry.mjs --check enforces schema, git sha resolvability, and both-direction train cross-checks with stable MT_ACCEPT_* error codes; tests/renderer/acceptance-registry.test.js wraps it so the standard vitest matrix (and thus CI) runs it.

tools/build-test-artifact.mjs takes --item --platform, derives the isolated identity from the head sha, writes a temporary merge config (never touching tracked files), shells the tauri build, digests the binary, smoke-launches and appends the artifact to the registry; --dry-run prints the merged config.
Trains README Acceptance row links the registry; M-046 SummaryDelta and a V-M-046 scenario describe the new gate; grace lint zero errors.

C-1.Name: Registry vs train drift
C-1.Expected: The validator fails closed in both directions: a train-accepted item without a matching registry verdict, or a registry-accepted item without train admission, both raise MT_ACCEPT_REGISTRY_MISMATCH.

C-2.Name: Pending item without artifact
C-2.Expected: A repaired-pending train item must carry an artifact-offered event or an explicit notApplicable/blocked reason (FIX-013: tooling; FIX-014: polygon offline with options) — ambiguity is an error.

C-3.Name: Rejected / sent back for rework
C-3.Expected: The rejection event records the owner's reason and the rework destination (wave/PR); the item's survey state reads "rework" with the date — the "why did we send it back" question stays answerable forever.

C-4.Name: Partial acceptance
C-4.Expected: A verdict lists exact accepted scenarios; unlisted scenarios of the same artifact are not accepted (the train README rule) and the registry keeps the item partially accepted, not queued, until the train admission records its scope.

C-5.Name: Artifact wiped from target/
C-5.Expected: The registry keeps identity, digest and build recipe; rebuilds via the builder reproduce an equivalent artifact and are recorded as new entries, never overwriting history.

C-6.Name: Owner verdict arrives in chat
C-6.Expected: The recording agent transcribes verdicts verbatim-scoped into the registry within the same session; a stated verdict that never lands in the registry is a protocol breach the next --check cannot see — the ledger's "last synced" line makes the gap visible.

C-7.Name: Security
C-7.Expected: No personal paths in the registry (bundle locations use repo-relative or well-known dirs); digests are public evidence; the builder never touches tracked files or signing material.

C-8.Name: Performance
C-8.Expected: --check stays under 2s (pure JSON + git cat-file); the builder is manual-only, never in CI.

Correctness.Note: The registry is additive bookkeeping; the train stays the admission authority and the validator enforces consistency in both directions, so a divergent edit fails CI rather than silently forking the truth. Event lists are append-only by convention; corrections append a superseding event instead of editing history.

Security.Note: No secrets; artifact digests and git shas are public evidence; builder output paths are repo-relative; no signing material involved (debug bundles are unsigned and isolated by identity).

UX.Note: The survey answers the owner's exact question in one table (item → state → artifact → verdict date → why-not, when applicable); the lifecycle mirrors the train stage names so there is exactly one vocabulary.

Performance.Note: Validator is JSON + git plumbing; the vitest wrapper runs in the existing matrix with no new CI surface.
